decision: Does the TensorLBM D2Q9 BGK + Guo-forcing + half-way bounce-back channel reproduce the OSS reference implementation (lettuce single-phase Poiseuille baseline skeleton) and the exact plane-Poiseuille solution within the owner 15 % band, when both codes are run at IDENTICAL lattice numbers, and which of the two forcing formulations / wall conventions is responsible for the residual difference?

artifacts_read: examples/simple_flows/Poiseuille.ipynb (baseline parameters: resolution=16, Re=1, Ma=0.02, BGK + ShanChen, zeros init, energy-based convergence)
oss_reference.executed: yes -- the OSS code is executed (CPU, double precision) from the checkout recorded per-arm in results; not a semantics-only port

alternatives.A1_oss_binary: the OSS implementation itself, run as shipped (PoiseuilleFlow2D + ShanChen force + BGKCollision), double precision, zeros initial condition, periodic streamwise, bounce-back walls
alternatives.A2_tensorlbm: TensorLBM in-repo D2Q9 BGK + Guo(2002) forcing + half-way bounce-back, single-layer reduction of verification/layered_poiseuille.solver, same nx=ny=resolution, same nu_lu / a_lu / init
alternatives.A3_exact: exact steady solution nu u'' = -g, u(0)=u(H)=0 with H = resolution-2 (half-way walls), evaluated at the fluid node centres; independently coded twice (closed-form parabola in tensorlbm.verification.xval.poiseuille_skeleton.analytic_profile and the general N-layer linear solve in verification/layered_poiseuille/analytic.solve_layered) and required to agree to 1e-12 relative
alternatives.rejected_alternative: a semantics-only port of the OSS lines (what the previous NEBB XVAL had to do when no GPU was available) -- rejected because here the OSS code is importable on CPU, so a real run-vs-run comparison is available

hypothesis: H1: at every active arm both codes stay within 15 % of the exact profile on all KPIs, both codes agree with each other within 15 %, and the error decreases with resolution. H1b (mechanism): the residual OSS-vs-TensorLBM difference at the OSS skeleton's own force level (Ma_peak ~2.5e-6) is dominated by the forcing formulation (ShanChen without a source term vs Guo with the (1-omega/2) source term) and grows linearly in the lattice force. H0 (falsifier): any KPI error >= 15 %, or the two codes disagreeing by >= 15 %, or the error not decreasing with resolution, or the geometry check (H_eff = resolution-2 +- 0.01) failing.

metrics.eps_inf: max|u_num - u_exact| / max|u_exact| over the fluid node rows of the x-averaged profile at the final steady snapshot
metrics.q_err: |Q_num - Q_exact| / Q_exact with Q = trapezoid(u dy) over the fluid samples (identical discrete functional both sides); the continuum flux g H^3/(12 nu) is reported separately as q_continuum and must be approached from the same side by both codes
metrics.y_peak_abs: |y(argmax u_num) - y(argmax u_exact)| in lattice units
metrics.shape_err: max|u_num/max(u_num) - u_exact/max(u_exact)|, separates shape from amplitude error
metrics.tv_rel_l2_rel_peak_ratio: symmetric OSS-vs-TensorLBM differences normalised by the mean of the two peaks (tv_rel = max-norm, l2_rel = L2 norm, peak_ratio = peak_TL/peak_OSS)
metrics.h_eff_max_dev: geometry check: max_i |H_i - H| with H_i = y_i + 2 nu u_i/(g y_i) over the fluid rows
metrics.steps_wall: march length and wall time per arm (evidence that the steady criterion was met, not truncated)

unit_of_analysis: one arm = one (resolution, viscosity mode, lattice force, initial condition, dtype) combination; KPIs are scalars plus one cross-section profile in lattice units

baseline_control.physical_reference: A3 exact parabola (two independent codings, cross-checked in the analysis step to <=1e-12 relative)
baseline_control.numerical_control_1: the OSS binary itself (A1) -- the reference implementation's own numbers, so the comparison is code-vs-code and not model-vs-model
baseline_control.numerical_control_2: N32/N48 (viscosity frozen at the res=16 value) vs V32/V48 (viscosity following the OSS rule): separates grid discretisation from the viscosity change that the OSS Re/Ma rule implies
baseline_control.numerical_control_3: D1/D4 (float32 vs float64 at the same parameters) and I16 (analytic init vs zeros init)
baseline_control.exclusion: the OSS analytic_solution evaluates the parabola at the solid rows too, where it returns a small NEGATIVE velocity (-13.8 % of the peak at res=16); KPI samples are restricted to fluid rows for BOTH codes, which is declared, not silently applied

predeclared_thresholds.convergence_rule: eps_inf must not increase from res 16 -> 32 -> 48 by more than a factor 1.2 (half-way bounce-back + Guo forcing is at best second order; a non-decreasing trend falsifies H1)
predeclared_thresholds.pass_rule: PASS iff every active arm with a converged march has eps_inf, eps_l2_rel, q_err, u_peak_err < 15 % AND |H_eff - H| < 0.01 AND the convergence rule holds; 3 % is reported as the target, not used to gate
predeclared_thresholds.no_post_hoc_tuning: the thresholds above are the owner standard (15 %) plus the predeclared 3 % target; they were not modified after inspecting any production result

stopping_rule: every arm marches in windows of 200 steps and stops when max|u(n)-u(n-200)|/max|u(n)| < 1e-6 (identical criterion for both codes) or at the per-arm max_steps; wall-clock cap 900 s per arm, an arm exceeding it is reported incomplete rather than re-tuned. No arm is extended or shortened after looking at its KPIs.
variables_changed: arm family verbatim: resolution 16 / 32 / 48 with the OSS Re=1, Ma=0.02 rule (nu_lu = (res-1) cs Ma / Re)
arm family refine: resolution 32 / 48 with nu_lu frozen at the res=16 value
arm family forcing: lattice force x1 / x1e2 / x1e3 / x1e4 at res=16 (Ma_peak 2.5e-6 -> 2.5e-2)
arm family dtype: float32 vs float64 (OSS arm) at force x1 and x1e4
arm family init: zeros vs analytic initial condition (TensorLBM arm)
variables_held_fixed: D2Q9 stencil, BGK/SRT collision (one relaxation time)
channels walls = half-way bounce-back at both y walls; streamwise periodic
nx = ny = resolution for both codes (the OSS skeleton is a square domain)
KPI sampling on fluid node rows only, x-averaged profile
double precision unless the arm says float32
TensorLBM forcing: Guo (2002) with velocity shift u = (sum f c + F/2)/rho
confounders: forcing formulation differs by construction (OSS ShanChen without source term, TensorLBM Guo) -- the F-family arms are the designed probe, so the baseline comparison is NOT a pure differencing of the two codes' force schemes
OSS streamwise axis is axis 0 (walls on axis 1) while TensorLBM stores (q, ny, nx): an axis mix-up reads as a ~14 % wall-row artefact, not as a physics difference
OSS analytic_solution is evaluated on the wall rows as well (negative velocity there); including them adds ~13.8 % to eps_inf at res=16

round-off floor: at the OSS skeleton's own force the lattice velocity is ~1.3e-6, i.e. ~1e-5 of the populations, so float32 populations cannot represent it (predeclared as a confounder, measured by arms D1/D4)
machine/thread nondeterminism: both codes are deterministic per step, but no bitwise claim is made (different summation orders)
repetition_rationale: both codes are deterministic: the march is a fixed-point iteration, not a sample, so repetition would only measure floating-point summation-order noise. Instead of repeats, three designed replications are used: (i) three resolutions with the same rule, (ii) two viscosity modes at the same resolution, (iii) four force levels; each pair isolates one factor. Uncertainty is therefore reported as the spread across the designed replications and as the round-off floor measured by the float32 arms, not as a standard error over repeats.

environment.tensorlbm: in-tree src/ (editable path insertion, no install)
environment.hardware: single node, single process, no cluster queue (total budget < 10 min wall)

analysis_plan: results/arms.json -> analyze.py builds (a) parameter table with all dimensionless numbers per arm, (b) per-arm error table vs the exact reference for both codes with PASS/FAIL against 15 % and the 3 % target, (c) OSS-vs-TensorLBM difference table, (d) resolution-trend fit log(eps_inf) vs log(H) for both codes and both viscosity modes, (e) force-level trend of both codes' eps_inf and of the cross-code difference, (f) dtype and init tables. Figures: profile comparison with error, log-log convergence, force sensitivity, field/difference maps. No outlier removal; arms that hit max_steps or the wall cap are reported as incomplete and excluded from the PASS claim but shown in the tables.
interpretation_limits: the comparison is a single-phase, steady, low-Reynolds (Re_H <= ~2) plane channel: it cannot certify unsteady, 3-D or multi-phase behaviour
the two codes differ in forcing scheme by construction, so 'the codes agree' does not mean 'the schemes are equivalent'
at the OSS skeleton's own force the problem is in the Stokes limit, where many scheme errors are invisible; the F-family arms are required before drawing conclusions about the forcing scheme
the OSS skeleton's Re=1/Ma=0.02 with Res=16 is an under-resolved demo configuration, not an accuracy benchmark of the OSS project
quantity claimed: profile, flux and peak of the developed single-phase channel; NOT wall shear stress evaluation order or transient behaviour
honest_disclosure: Before this file was written, two single-arm scratch runs (one per code, res=16, OSS parameters) were executed to verify that the OSS import chain works on CPU and that the in-repo kernel accepts the OSS lattice numbers; they revealed the wall-row artefact of the OSS analytic (see confounders) and the correct wall-normal axis. No threshold, arm or metric was changed as a result; the 15 % acceptance band and 3 % target are the owner standards and were fixed from the start.
